title: Android Kotlin
description: Beginner-to-advanced Android application reference covering Kotlin essentials, platform components, lifecycle, state, target-SDK compatibility, edge-to-edge and adaptive UI, intents, permissions, storage, offline-first sync, and scalable app architecture.

sections.title: Kotlin Essentials for Android
sections.description: Use Kotlin's type system to make Android boundaries explicit and safe.

subtopics.title: Null Safety & Platform Boundaries
subtopics.description: Model absence with nullable types, narrow once, and avoid assertions at lifecycle and Java interop boundaries.

codeBlocks.code:
val userId: String = intent.getStringExtra(EXTRA_USER_ID)
    ?: return finish()

val title = user?.displayName.orEmpty()
val avatar = user?.avatarUrl?.let(imageLoader::load)

requireNotNull(savedState[KEY_ACCOUNT_ID]) { "Missing account id" }

annotations.text: Fail or exit at the boundary so the rest of the function uses a non-null value.
Run an operation only when the receiver is non-null.

callouts.title: Avoid !!
callouts.text: Lifecycle timing, missing Bundle keys, Java platform types, and process recreation make non-null assertions fragile. Validate at boundaries or model a loading/absent state.

subtopics.title: data, sealed, enum & value Types
subtopics.description: Use data classes for immutable values, sealed hierarchies for closed alternatives, enums for fixed constants, and value classes to prevent primitive confusion.

callouts.title: Prefer Impossible States to Be Unrepresentable
callouts.text: A sealed state prevents contradictory flags such as loading=true and error!=null. A data class is better when states can coexist independently.

subtopics.title: Extensions, Delegation & Scope Functions
subtopics.description: Use extensions for discoverable boundary helpers, delegation for reusable behavior, and scope functions only when the receiver/result distinction stays obvious.

callouts.title: Extensions Are Statically Dispatched
callouts.text: An extension does not modify or virtually override the receiver type. Prefer an injected collaborator when behavior needs state, substitution, or polymorphism.

sections.title: Android Components & Process Model
sections.description: Know which platform component owns entry, UI, background, and cross-app work.

subtopics.title: Activity, Service, Receiver & Provider
subtopics.description: Activities host user-facing windows; services perform user-visible ongoing work; receivers handle brief broadcasts; providers expose structured data across process boundaries.

codeBlocks.code:
Activity: screen/window entry point; can be recreated at any time
Foreground service: ongoing user-noticeable work with notification
BroadcastReceiver: short event handler; schedule longer work
ContentProvider: URI-based data contract, often cross-process
WorkManager: persistent deferrable work with constraints
ViewModel: screen state/business-logic holder, not a platform component

callouts.title: The Process Is Disposable
callouts.text: Android may kill a background process without calling a final callback. Persist durable state as it changes; never rely on an Application singleton as permanent storage.

subtopics.title: Context & Memory Ownership
subtopics.description: Activity context carries UI configuration and window identity; application context follows the process and must not own screen objects.

callouts.title: Do Not Store Activities
callouts.text: Long-lived objects retaining Activity, Fragment, View, binding, or callback references leak an obsolete UI after configuration changes.

sections.title: Lifecycle, Configuration & State Restoration
sections.description: Match every value and task to the lifetime it must survive.

subtopics.title: Lifecycle Ownership
subtopics.description: Lifecycle callbacks describe transitions, not guaranteed paired events. Use lifecycle-aware APIs and keep callbacks small.

diagram.content:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Created: onCreate
  Created --> Started: onStart
  Started --> Resumed: onResume
  Resumed --> Started: onPause
  Started --> Created: onStop
  Created --> [*]: onDestroy

callouts.title: onDestroy Is Not Persistence
callouts.text: Process death may bypass cleanup callbacks. Persist important user data immediately or transactionally; use callbacks only to release resources while the process remains alive.

subtopics.title: ViewModel, Saved State & Persistent Storage
subtopics.description: Choose storage by lifetime, size, and source of truth rather than convenience.

table.title: Android State Survival Matrix
rows: Small UI state such as input and selection
Authoritative durable application or preference data

codeBlocks.code:
Configuration change only → ViewModel
Process recreation, small UI input/key → SavedStateHandle / saved-state APIs
App restart, user/application data → Room, DataStore, file, or server
Large/complex state → persist canonical data; save only an ID or query
Ephemeral derived UI → recompute from source of truth

callouts.title: ViewModel Does Not Survive Process Death
callouts.text: A ViewModel survives owner recreation such as rotation, not system process termination. SavedStateHandle is for small reconstruction inputs, not a database replacement.

subtopics.title: SavedStateHandle
subtopics.description: Store small, serializable inputs needed to reconstruct screen state after process recreation.

callouts.title: Save Reconstruction Inputs
callouts.text: Save the query or entity ID, then reload canonical records. Saving whole object graphs risks transaction-size failures and stale duplicated data.

sections.title: Intents, Results, Deep Links & Permissions
sections.description: Treat every platform or external-app boundary as untrusted input.

subtopics.title: Explicit & Implicit Intents
subtopics.description: Use explicit intents for known in-app components and implicit intents for capabilities another app may handle.

codeBlocks.code:
val internal = Intent(this, DetailActivity::class.java)
    .putExtra(EXTRA_ITEM_ID, itemId.value)

val share = Intent(Intent.ACTION_SEND).apply {
    type = "text/plain"
    putExtra(Intent.EXTRA_TEXT, publicUrl)
}
startActivity(Intent.createChooser(share, getString(R.string.share_with)))

callouts.title: Validate Incoming Data
callouts.text: Intent extras, URIs, ClipData, and deep-link parameters can be absent, malformed, oversized, or attacker-controlled. Parse into domain types before use.

subtopics.title: Activity Results & Photo Picker
subtopics.description: Register contracts during initialization, use the system Photo Picker for user-selected media, and keep result handling separate from launching.

callouts.title: Choose the Narrowest Contract
callouts.text: Use Photo Picker for selected photos/videos without broad media permission. If a document URI must survive restart, use an appropriate OpenDocument contract and persistable URI permission.

subtopics.title: Runtime Permission Flow
subtopics.description: Ask in context, explain value, handle denial gracefully, and request only permissions required by the current platform behavior.

callouts.title: Denial Is a Valid State
callouts.text: Users may deny permanently or policy may restrict access. The app must remain usable where possible and should not loop or pressure the user. Notification, media, nearby-device, and location rules differ by API level, so gate both requests and behavior.

subtopics.title: Target SDK & Platform Behavior Changes
subtopics.description: Treat every target SDK upgrade as a compatibility project: read both all-app and target-specific behavior changes, then test affected journeys on that platform.

table.title: Modern Android Compatibility Watchlist
rows: Notification permission, Photo Picker, media access
Request only when needed; prefer picker-based access
Foreground-service types, exact alarms, background starts
Declare valid types and verify scheduling eligibility
Handle system bars, cutouts, gesture and IME insets
Predictive back defaults; edge-to-edge opt-out removed
Use supported back APIs and test all back destinations
Large-screen adaptation, local-network and other behavior changes
Run preview compatibility tests; do not ship preview assumptions as stable contracts

callouts.title: Compile SDK Is Not Target SDK
callouts.text: compileSdk exposes APIs; targetSdk opts the app into platform behavior changes. Keep minSdk fallbacks explicit and test the actual targetSdk configuration used for release.

sections.title: Resources, Localization & Configuration
sections.description: Keep user-facing values in resources and design for runtime configuration changes.

subtopics.title: Resource Types & Qualifiers
subtopics.description: Use strings, plurals, dimensions, colors, drawables, and qualified alternatives so Android selects the best resource for locale, density, size, and night mode.

codeBlocks.code:
val message = resources.getQuantityString(
    R.plurals.download_count,
    count,
    count
)
val spacing = resources.getDimensionPixelSize(R.dimen.content_spacing)

callouts.title: Do Not Concatenate Sentences
callouts.text: Word order and plural rules vary by language. Use formatted string/plural resources with translator context rather than assembling user-visible fragments in Kotlin.

subtopics.title: Configuration & Adaptive UI
subtopics.description: Rotation, resize, locale, font scale, density, theme, and device posture can change while the app runs.

codeBlocks.code:
Avoid caching configuration-derived values globally
Use dp for layout and sp for scalable text
Draw edge-to-edge and consume system-bar, cutout, gesture, and IME insets
Use current window size/posture and canonical layouts, not device-name checks
Test resize, multi-window, desktop windowing, fold posture, keyboard/mouse, large fonts, and long translations
Let Activities recreate unless a proven platform integration requires manual handling

callouts.title: Recreation Is a Correctness Test
callouts.text: Regularly enable developer options that destroy activities and test rotation/resizing. Bugs found there often reveal misplaced ownership or missing persistence.

sections.title: Data, Storage & Background Work
sections.description: Select persistence and scheduling tools based on data shape, consistency, durability, and user visibility.

subtopics.title: Room, DataStore, Files & Cache
subtopics.description: Room fits relational/queryable data; DataStore fits small settings; files fit opaque or streamed data; cache is disposable and must have a source of truth.

codeBlocks.code:
Relational entities, joins, migrations → Room
Typed preferences or small settings → DataStore
Media/documents/blobs → files or platform document storage
Temporary reproducible data → cache directory
Sensitive secrets → platform-backed secure design; minimize storage
Cross-device canonical data → server plus explicit offline strategy

callouts.title: Migrations Are Product Code
callouts.text: Test schema and preference migrations against real historical versions. Destructive fallback can erase user data and should be an explicit product decision.

subtopics.title: Offline-First Source of Truth & Sync
subtopics.description: For data that must remain usable without reliable connectivity, expose local persisted data as the read source and reconcile network updates through an explicit sync policy.

diagram.content:
flowchart LR
  UI[UI observes] --> R[Repository]
  R --> L[Local source of truth]
  N[Network] --> S[Sync and conflict policy]
  S --> L
  W[Durable WorkManager queue] --> S

codeBlocks.code:
Reads → observe the local source of truth
Refresh → fetch, validate, then update local storage transactionally
Critical offline write → save locally, enqueue durable sync, expose pending state
Conflict → define server-wins, client-wins, merge, or user resolution
Retry → bounded backoff with idempotency and observable failure

callouts.title: Connectivity Is a Hint
callouts.text: A network callback cannot guarantee that a request will succeed. Attempt operations under policy, handle failures, and let durable work retry when constraints are satisfied.

subtopics.title: Coroutine, WorkManager, Alarm or Foreground Service
subtopics.description: Use a coroutine for in-process lifetime-bound work, WorkManager for persistent deferrable jobs, alarms for precise user-facing time semantics when allowed, and foreground services for ongoing noticeable work.

codeBlocks.code:
Needed only while screen exists → ViewModel/lifecycle coroutine
Must finish eventually after app exit → WorkManager
Periodic best-effort maintenance → periodic WorkManager
Exact calendar/user alarm → alarm APIs and current permission rules
Ongoing user-noticeable operation → foreground service + notification

callouts.title: Background Limits Change
callouts.text: Android background execution and permission rules evolve. Check official guidance for your target SDK before shipping scheduling, alarms, or foreground services.

sections.title: Architecture, Security & Production Readiness
sections.description: Scale through clear ownership and boundaries, not layers added by habit.

subtopics.title: UI, Data & Optional Domain Layers
subtopics.description: The UI renders state and sends actions; repositories expose application data; use cases are valuable when business logic is reused or a ViewModel becomes complex.

diagram.content:
flowchart LR
  UI[UI: state + user actions] --> VM[Screen ViewModel]
  VM --> UC[Optional use cases]
  VM --> R[Repository]
  UC --> R
  R --> L[Local source]
  R --> N[Network source]
  R --> P[Platform source]

callouts.title: Single Source of Truth
callouts.text: Choose one authoritative owner for each piece of data. Other layers observe or derive it rather than maintaining unsynchronized copies.

subtopics.title: Dependency Injection & Boundaries
subtopics.description: Prefer constructor injection. Use Hilt when component graph complexity warrants it; manual composition is sufficient for small apps.

callouts.title: Inject Behavior, Not Service Locators
callouts.text: Passing Context, a container, or a global singleton deep into business code hides dependencies. Inject the narrow API the class needs.

subtopics.title: Production Checklist
subtopics.description: Audit boundary validation, exported components, lifecycle ownership, state restoration, accessibility, performance, and observability.

codeBlocks.code:
□ All-app and target-SDK behavior changes are reviewed
□ External Intent/URI/provider input is validated
□ Exported components and package visibility are intentional
□ Runtime permissions are requested in context with denial paths
□ Secrets and sensitive logs are minimized
□ UI objects are not retained by long-lived owners
□ Durable state is persisted before process death
□ Edge-to-edge, predictive back, resize, locale, night mode, and large fonts work
□ Blocking/CPU work never stalls the main thread
□ Offline, denial, empty, loading, and retry states are designed
□ App startup, jank, ANRs, and critical journeys are measured
□ Errors have actionable telemetry without personal data
□ Tests cover ViewModels, repositories, migrations, navigation, and platform upgrades

callouts.title: Related Deep Dives
callouts.text: Use the dedicated Coroutines, Flows, Compose, Modifiers, Testing, Collections, and Naming sheets for mechanics intentionally excluded here.
